meta.titre: Map Bearings and Direction: compass points, three-figure bearings, back bearings and grid references
meta.sous_theme: Compass directions, bearings, back bearings and six-figure grid references on a topographic map

sections.contenu_markdown: A guide at the foot of Mount Cameroon opens a map, finds the village where the group will sleep and says, "We shall walk north-east, on a bearing of about 045 degrees." In one sentence he has used direction and bearing. Paper 2 gives a topographic map and asks for the direction and bearing of one place from another, for grid references of features and for distances. These questions follow fixed steps, so careful practice turns them into sure marks.

items: North is at the top of a topographic map, east to the right, south at the bottom and west to the left.
A full turn is 360 degrees and a right angle is 90 degrees.
A protractor measures angles in degrees, and a ruler measures lengths in centimetres.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Direction and bearing
A **direction** is given by compass points. A **bearing** is the angle measured **clockwise from north**, written with **three figures** and a degree sign.

| Compass point | N | NE | E | SE | S | SW | W | NW |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bearing | 000° | 045° | 090° | 135° | 180° | 225° | 270° | 315° |

### Measuring the bearing of B from A
1. Find the place you start **from** (A) and the place you go **to** (B).
2. Join A to B with a light pencil line and extend it a little.
3. Draw a north line through A, parallel to the vertical grid lines.
4. Put the centre of the protractor on A and its zero on the north line.
5. Read the angle clockwise from the north line to line AB.
6. Write it with three figures, for example 075°.

### Back bearing
The bearing of A from B is the **back bearing**. Add 180° if the bearing is less than 180°; subtract 180° if it is more than 180°. The bearing of B from A is 070°, so the bearing of A from B is 250°.

### Six-figure grid reference
The first three figures give the easting: the vertical line, then tenths of the way to the next line. The last three figures give the northing in the same way. Always **eastings first**, then northings. In 347512, the position is 34 plus seven tenths along, and 51 plus two tenths up.

### Types of north
**True north** points to the North Pole, **magnetic north** is where a compass needle points, and **grid north** is the direction of the vertical grid lines.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says direction or asks which way
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use the eight compass points and always say *from where*: *the market is north-west of the school*. Do not give a bearing when only a direction is asked, and do not give only a compass point when the question asks for a bearing.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks for both, as in State the direction and bearing of A from B
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give the compass point first and the bearing next, for example: **south-east, 135°**. If you measured 128°, the nearest compass point is south-east, so the two parts agree.

variantes.nom: Length of a road and area on the map
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question mixes direction with distance or area
variantes.contenu_markdown: For a curved road, lay a thread along the road, straighten it, measure it with a ruler and apply the scale. For area, count the grid squares more than half inside the shape as whole squares and ignore smaller parts. Check what each square is worth from the grid spacing and the scale.

sections.enonce_markdown:
On a map of scale 1 : 50,000 the grid lines are 1 km apart. Taking the school as the origin, the church is 3 km east and 3 km north, the hospital is 3 km west and 3 km north of the school.
(a) State the direction and the bearing of the church from the school.
(b) Give the bearing of the school from the church.
(c) The hospital is due west of the church. Give the bearing of the church from the hospital.
(d) How far apart are the school and the church on the ground and on the map?

etapes.action: Compare the east and north distances for part (a).
etapes.justification: When a place is as far east as it is north, it lies exactly midway between north and east.

etapes.action: Find the back bearing for part (b).
etapes.justification: The bearing of the school from the church is the opposite direction. 045° is less than 180°, so add 180°.

etapes.action: Use the west-east line for part (c).
etapes.justification: The hospital is due west of the church, so the church is due east of the hospital.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The bearing of the church from the hospital is **090°**.

etapes.justification: Both east and north distances are 3 km, so the straight line is the hypotenuse: $\sqrt{3^2 + 3^2}$ km. On a 1 : 50,000 map 1 km is 2 cm.
etapes.resultat_markdown: $\sqrt{18} \approx 4.24$ km on the ground; $4.24 \times 2 \approx 8.5$ cm on the map.

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) North-east, 045°. (b) 225°. (c) 090°. (d) About **4.2 km** on the ground, or about **8.5 cm** on the map.

items.erreur_markdown: Measuring the bearing from the wrong place, for example measuring the bearing of B from A with the protractor on B.
items.pourquoi_faux: The protractor must be at the place the bearing is taken **from**. Measuring from B gives the back bearing.
items.correction_markdown: Put the protractor at **A** to read the bearing of B from A.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing a bearing as 45° or N45°E.
items.pourquoi_faux: A bearing uses three figures and is measured clockwise from north.

items.erreur_markdown: Finding the back bearing of 250° as 250° + 180° = 430°.
items.pourquoi_faux: A bearing never exceeds 360°. For a bearing above 180° you subtract 180°.

items.erreur_markdown: Measuring the angle from the edge of the page instead of from a north line drawn through the starting point.
items.pourquoi_faux: The edge of the paper may not point to north. The zero of the protractor must lie along a line parallel to the vertical grid lines.
items.correction_markdown: Draw a **north line through the starting point** using the grid lines.

items.erreur_markdown: Giving a grid reference with the northing first.
items.pourquoi_faux: Eastings (along the bottom) always come before northings (up the side).
items.correction_markdown: Read **along the corridor, then up the stairs**.

items.enonce_markdown: Give the bearing for each direction: north-east, south, west, north-west. Give the compass point for the bearings 090° and 225°.
items.solution_markdown: North-east **045°**; south **180°**; west **270°**; north-west **315°**. The bearing 090° is **east**; 225° is **south-west**.

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) Find the back bearing of each of these bearings: 072°, 130°, 238°, 305°.
(b) A spot height lies three tenths of the way east between grid lines 27 and 28, and eight tenths of the way north between lines 54 and 55. Write its six-figure grid reference.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) 072° + 180° = **252°**; 130° + 180° = **310°**; 238° - 180° = **058°**; 305° - 180° = **125°**.
(b) Easting 27 and three tenths gives 273; northing 54 and eight tenths gives 548. The reference is **273548**.

items.enonce_markdown:
On a map of scale 1 : 50,000 with grid lines 1 km apart, a river bridge lies 4 km east and 4 km north of a village. A clinic lies 6 km due south of the bridge.
(a) State the direction and bearing of the bridge from the village.
(b) Give the bearing of the clinic from the bridge and the bearing of the bridge from the clinic.
(c) Calculate the distance on the ground from the village to the bridge, and the distance in centimetres between them on the map.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Equal east and north distances, so the direction is **north-east** and the bearing **045°**.
(b) The clinic is due south of the bridge: **180°**. The back bearing is $180 - 180 = 0$, so the bridge is **000°** from the clinic.
(c) Distance $= \sqrt{4^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{32} \approx 5.66$ km, about **5.7 km** on the ground. On the map 1 km is 2 cm, so $5.66 \times 2 \approx 11.3$ cm, about **11.3 cm**.

items_markdown: A bearing is an angle measured clockwise from north and written with three figures; north is 000°, east 090°, south 180° and west 270°.
The bearing of B from A starts at A: put the protractor at A, with zero on a north line drawn parallel to the grid lines.
Back bearing: add 180° if the bearing is below 180°, subtract 180° if it is above.
Grid references give eastings first, then northings; in six figures the third and sixth figures are tenths.
Give the direction as a compass point and the bearing as three figures, and make sure the two agree.
On a 1 : 50,000 map 1 km on the ground is 2 cm on the map.
